summary: This RFC defines YANG data models for bearers and for attachment circuits as a service. A bearer is the underlying link; the AC is the setup needed for data exchange over it.

eli5.summary: Ordering a connection like an online order: this describes the order forms for the physical line and the setup.

questions: what is a bearer in networking
subtitle: YANG service models that let a customer order the physical link (bearer) and the setup over it (attachment circuit) from a provider.

tldr.problem: Before a network service can run, the link between a customer and the provider needs a matching setup on both sides, and that setup often crosses organizational boundaries with no standard way to ask for it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two YANG service modules: ietf-bearer-svc to manage bearers (the underlying links) and ietf-ac-svc to manage attachment circuits (the setup over them), with a bearer reference tying the two together.
tldr.outcome: Services such as VPNs or RFC 9543 Network Slice Services can be bound to ACs that were ordered separately, so AC details live in one model instead of being repeated in every service model.

facts.label: Reserved ASN for customers with no ASN

today: RFC 9834 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2025. It has not been obsoleted or updated. It is used together with the network model in RFC 9835 and the VPN augmentations in RFC 9836.

sections.title: The Problem: Links and Their Setup
sections.content:
Networks deliver connectivity to customers through termination points such as Customer Edges (CEs), peer border routers, data center gateways or Internet Exchange Points. For data to flow, the links between those points and the provider network (usually a Provider Edge, or PE) need the right setup. The RFC calls that setup an attachment circuit (AC) and the underlying link a bearer.

Creating an AC means coordinating endpoints that may belong to different administrative entities. Management systems on both sides must agree on resources such as Layer 2 tags, the IP address family or IP subnets. The RFC calls offering this as a programmable interface Attachment Circuits as a Service (ACaaS).

The document favors relying completely on the AC service model instead of copying AC data nodes into each advanced service model. That way, upgrades (new encryption schemes, additional routing protocols) happen in one place.
sections.eli5: A bearer is the road, and an attachment circuit is the traffic rules on that road. Both sides must agree on the rules before cars can drive, so this RFC gives them a standard way to agree.

sections.title: Key Terms: Bearer, AC, CE and PE
sections.content:
A bearer is a physical or logical link that connects a customer node or site to a provider network. It can be wireless or wired and can be built from one or several technologies, for example a Link Aggregation Group (LAG). The operator allocates a unique bearer reference that a customer can later use to say exactly where a service is to be bound. Several ACs may share one bearer, for example multiple VLANs on one physical link.

A CE is equipment dedicated to a customer and connected to one or more PEs via ACs. A PE is provider-owned equipment at the edge of the service network. The RFC also defines a Parent AC and Parent Bearer: other ACs or bearers (children) are built from them and inherit their properties.

A service orchestrator talks to the customer and is typically responsible for ACs, PE selection and asking a network controller to activate the service.
sections.eli5: The customer's box is the CE and the provider's box is the PE. A bearer is the wire between them. A parent is like a master recipe that child recipes copy from.

sections.title: How the AC Models Fit Together
sections.content:
Five YANG modules make up the AC family. ietf-ac-common (RFC 9833) holds shared pieces and is imported by ietf-bearer-svc, ietf-ac-svc and ietf-ac-ntw. The last of these is the network model in RFC 9835. The ietf-ac-glue module in RFC 9836 augments the L2VPN and L3VPN service and network models with AC references.

This RFC's AC model is a service model, not a network model and not a device model. It does not expose which PE node terminates an AC; that mapping stays inside the provider's network controllers. Those node-specific details appear in the network model instead.

The RFC explains why existing VPN models were not reused. The L2VPN Service Model (L2SM, RFC 8466) does not cover Layer 3 provisioning. The L3VPN Service Model (L3SM, RFC 8299) does not sufficiently address Layer 2 and, for example, cannot provision multiple BGP peer groups over the same AC.
sections.eli5: There is a customer-facing order form (this RFC), a provider-side work sheet (the next RFC), and some glue that connects them to VPN forms. The customer never sees which exact machine the provider uses.

sections.title: Typical Deployments
sections.content:
A CE can be a physical device or a logical entity such as a virtual service function. A single CE may terminate several ACs on the same or different bearers, and customers may ask for protection, such as ACs ending on the same PE or on distinct PEs. The provider uses such requests to choose where to terminate the AC and whether to turn on features such as VRRP.

AC provisioning can be separate from service provisioning. A customer first requests a bearer or AC, then refers to it when requesting services. One AC may host multiple connectivity services, and a provider may expose an interface to manage ACs network-wide to avoid service interference.

Resources such as Layer 2 or Layer 3 identifiers are typically imposed by the provider, but the customer may supply a specific one, for example from a pool the provider pre-provisioned. The provider may accept or reject it. The RFC also describes a recursive deployment in which a Service Broker acts as a server to the customer and as a client to the provider.
sections.eli5: You can order the road first and decide later what traffic will use it. You can even suggest your own house number, but the provider can say no.

sections.title: The Bearer Service Module
sections.content:
The ietf-bearer-svc module manages bearers: the properties of an attachment below Layer 3. A customer can first list available presence locations, filtered by customer name and AS number (the reserved value AS 0 is used for customers with no ASN), and then reference a location in a bearer request through provider-location-reference.

Each bearer has a client-chosen name. The provider returns a read-only bearer-reference that is used later in AC requests. Other nodes include type (Ethernet, wireless, LAG and so on), customer-point (a device, a site, or custom information), bearer-parent-ref for LAG members, and sync-phy-capable, sync-phy-enabled and sync-phy-type for synchronization such as SyncE. Timing can be requested with requested-start and requested-stop, and the provider reports actual-start and actual-stop.

Bearers can be created from scratch on request (greenfield creation, optionally with placement-constraints) or discovered from the network, for example through LLDP, and exposed through the same structure.

Each bearer has an admin-status (what the operator intends) and an oper-status (what is observed). The administrative setting MUST NOT be influenced by the operational state. A bearer that is administratively enabled but operationally down signals an anomaly.
sections.eli5: The bearer form is like ordering a phone line: you say where you are and what kind of line you want, and the provider gives you a line number to use on later forms.

sections.title: The Attachment Circuit Service Module
sections.content:
The ietf-ac-svc module is organized as shown in the tree below. Each AC has a name that is unique within a domain. Profiles are reusable: specific-provisioning-profiles list valid provider identifiers for encryption, QoS, failure detection, forwarding and routing policies, while service-provisioning-profiles list service profile identifiers. The model only carries identifiers; what a profile means is local to each provider. An ac-group-profile holds parameters shared by a set of ACs, and values set on an individual AC take precedence.

Per-AC nodes include role (for example UNI or NNI), peer-sap-id (the customer-side Service Attachment Points), group for redundancy or protection, and read-only service-ref and server-reference. A test-only flag requests a feasibility check without enforcement.

Parent and child ACs let stable common data live in a parent while children track dynamic information. When a parent is deleted, all its children MUST be deleted. A child MAY rely on more than one parent, but then those parents MUST NOT overlap.

An AC is then described by containers for l2-connection (encapsulation such as dot1q or QinQ, pseudowire, VPLS or VXLAN tunnels, and a bearer-reference), ip-connection (IPv4 and IPv6, dynamic or static addressing), routing-protocols (static, BGP, OSPF, IS-IS, RIP, VRRP), oam, security (encryption) and service (such as MTU and bandwidth). Features mark the conditional parts, so a deployment can support only what it needs.
sections.eli5: The AC form is a big checklist: how the link is labeled, what addresses to use, how routes are learned, how to check it is alive, and how to protect it. Shared checklists can be reused, and your own answers win over the shared ones.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modules are accessed through YANG-based protocols such as NETCONF and RESTCONF, which have to use a secure transport and mutual authentication. Servers MUST verify that a requesting client is entitled to access a given bearer or AC; a customer must not see another customer's bearers or ACs. NACM (RFC 8341) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

Writable nodes are sensitive. An attacker who can change placement-constraints, bearer or ac data could cause SLA violations or add or delete bearers and ACs. The provisioning profile containers are tagged nacm:default-deny-write.

Readable data can leak privacy-related information, such as customer names and locations, or Layer 2 and Layer 3 connection details that can be used to track a customer. Keying material is especially sensitive, since the keys could be used to inject spoofed routing advertisements. Keys are supplied as ASCII strings; a hexadecimal format is not included because the underlying device modules do not support it.
sections.eli5: The order system must check who is asking, because you should only be able to change your own orders and see your own details. Secret passwords in the orders need extra care.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered two XML namespace URIs, urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-bearer-svc and urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-ac-svc, in the IETF XML Registry. It also registered the two YANG modules in the YANG Module Names registry, with prefixes bearer-svc and ac-svc. Both are marked as not maintained by IANA.
sections.eli5: The two new forms were given official names in a public list so nobody else uses the same names.
